national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today distributed more than 51 thousand appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various Government Organisations at the 20th Rozgar Mela this afternoon through video conferencing. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Modi said that in recent years, the Central government has consistently focused on equipping the youth with the skills and opportunities needed to prepare for the future. He said the government’s endeavour has also been to ensure that the education and skills of the country’s youth keep pace with the needs of the changing economy. Prime Minister Modi said the government is also working to rapidly expand employment opportunities in the private sector. He said, with this objective, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana has been launched with an outlay of around one lakh crore. The scheme is expected to enable nearly two crore young people to enter the workforce for the first time. Mr Modi highlighted that under the initiative, the government is providing an incentive of up to 15 thousand rupees to youth securing their first jobs, while also incentivising employers to create additional employment opportunities. Prime Minister Modi said that India has signed Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries in the past few years, which is opening new doors of opportunity for the country’s youth. He said, such trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships and markets for country’s entrepreneurs, and create new career possibilities for the youth. He said, the talent and skills of country’s youth have won the trust of the entire world. Mr Modi said that the world has great expectations from India’s innovators, entrepreneurs and its youth power. Prime Minister Modi said that India is today the world’s third largest startup ecosystem. He highlighted that today, nearly half of recognised startups are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Mr Modi added that the youth from villages, towns, and smaller cities are playing a significant role in India’s new economy. The Prime Minister highlighted that young people from smaller cities are working on their ideas, founding new companies, and creating employment opportunities for others. On the occasion, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh said that an assessment of employment generation and recruitment through Rozgar Mela has shown that there has been a significant increase in government appointments, along with the greater transparency. He said that nearly ten lakh 96 thousand appointments were made during the ten years of the NDA government as compared to seven lakh 22 thousand appointments during UPA government through three major central recruitment agencies – Union Public Service Commission, the Staff Selection Commission and the Railway Recruitment Boards. The Minister said several measures have been taken to improve the recruitment system. The 20th Rozgar Mela was held at 45 locations across the country. The newly recruited candidates will be joining various Ministries and Departments of the Government of India including, Ministries of Finance, Railways, Home Affairs, Health and Family Welfare, and Defence, among others. With the 20th Rozgar Mela, a total of about 12 lakh 75 thousand youths have received appointment letters. The Rozgar Mela reflects the Government’s continued focus on creating employment opportunities for the youth and ensuring their greater participation in the country’s development journey.

national_raw_news.title: 4 mins ago | National 273 PM Modi says India’s per capita carbon emissions less than half of global average
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India’s contribution to per capita carbon emissions is less than half of the global average. Inaugurating the International Conference on the Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that developing countries have often been unfairly held responsible for carbon emissions. He highlighted that India is the only country in the G-20 that has successfully fulfilled the commitments made at the COP-21 Summit in Paris ahead of schedule. The Prime Minister said, over the past twelve years, India has made extraordinary progress in every field related to the environment. Prime Minister Modi said India is working with the rest of the world and setting new standards for environmental protection through initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance, Global Biofuels Alliance, International Big Cat Alliance and Mission LiFE. Mr Modi said that over the past twelve years, India has made extraordinary progress in every field related to the environment. The Prime Minister said, India’s major focus has been on renewable energy, and played a significant role in environmental protection. Prime Minister Modi said that India is rapidly working in areas like clean mobility and green hydrogen today. He highlighted that India’s wind energy capacity has witnessed three times growth in the last 12 years. Mr Modi emphasized that new India is also focusing on nuclear energy generation. On the occasion, Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant said that the idea of preserving the Earth existed in the country much before the emergence of environmental tribunals, regulatory mechanisms and compliance frameworks. He underlined the importance of the fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures. The Chief Justice said that India’s Constitution is not merely a political document but also a moral commitment towards past, present and future generations. Speaking on the occasion, Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav said that India’s approach to environmental responsibility is deeply rooted in its ancient civilizational ethos, which regards the Earth not as a possession but as a shared inheritance and a sacred trust. He said non-fossil fuel sources now account for more than 54 percent of India’s installed electricity capacity, surpassing the earlier target. Mr Yadav said India ranks third globally in renewable energy installed capacity and is the world’s second-largest solar growth market. Mr. Yadav added that these achievements demonstrate that economic growth and determined climate action can progress together. On wildlife conservation, the Minister said India’s efforts are not limited to protecting individual animals but are aimed at safeguarding the entire ecological balance. He said the populations of key species, including tigers, lions and elephants, have increased significantly, while efforts are also being intensified to conserve vultures and the Great Indian Bustard. Mr. Yadav also highlighted India’s efforts towards conservation and restoration of forests, grasslands and wetlands. The two-day conference is being organised by the National Green Tribunal. It has brought together environmental experts, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and District Court judges. It will also bring together eminent judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries. The Conference will provide a platform to exchange judicial approaches, scientific knowledge, environmental governance practices and institutional experiences. During the conference, participants will discuss key environmental and climate challenges, including gaps in policy formulation, implementation and enforcement. The conference will also explore ways to strengthen environmental governance and institutional cooperation.
